newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares fueled by world market,trend unclear.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares fueled by world market,trend unclear.

text.p: Foreign markets pushed up Russian shares on Thursday, traders said, though they saw no clear trend at home and said fundamentally the market had not changed.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index closed up for the first time since July 9 at 462.37, a 2.1 percent gain on Wednesday's close. Market volume was a healthy $66.47 million.
National energy company UES rose to $0.4129 from $0.3951, but the best gains were shown by less liquid shares such as Yuganskneftegaz which jumped to $31.00 from $25.50 in late trading on Wednesday.
Regional telecoms were also seen strong.

"The Brazilian market lent stability," said Renaissance Capital chief equity trader Anton Kudryashov. But he said the market was still volatile and declined to predict whether it would gain or fall on Friday.
Russian investors such as insurance companies, banks and mutual funds were adding firm tone to the market, he said.

"The wind is from the U.S. mostly," said Rye, Man and Gor Securities sales chief Kirill Maltsev, pointing to the Dow Jones which broke the 8,000 point mark on Wednesday on investor confidence over mild inflation and strong corporate profits.
He saw no trend for Russia but said buying had also been in response to Wednesday's fall which saw the RTS index lose about four percent. But he said buyers were so far tentative.

"I would not use the term bullish for this market," he said, adding investors were considering whether the consolidation which set in last week following a 30 percent gain over the previous month had now ended.
